scientific_question: Does severe reactive-astrocyte cuffing of CA1 pyramidal neurons, defined by multiple nearby reactive astrocytes rather than any single neighbor, better capture memory-decline signal than the current broader CA1 reactivity features?
rationale: The accepted panel has progressively improved as the CA1 astrocyte signal became more neuron-anchored, with the largest gain coming from the shift from astrocyte-centered summaries to pyramidal-neuron cuffing. The right next test is therefore a small threshold refinement within that same interaction family: ask whether multi-astrocyte cuffing is a cleaner disease-state readout than the current any-cuffing measure, potentially adding signal or replacing one weaker astrocyte-centric panel member.
approach: Assign cells to regions using CustomAnnotations polygons after dividing annotation coordinates by 16. Restrict to CA1 Pyramidal Neuron cells and CA1 Reactive Astrocyte cells. Using cell centroids, count for each CA1 pyramidal neuron how many CA1 reactive astrocytes lie within a 35 µm radius (convert to pixels using slide MPP from the paired SVS if available, otherwise use the cohort-typical ~0.503 µm/pixel). Compute the donor-level biomarker as the fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons whose nearby reactive-astrocyte count meets a severity threshold k. This keeps the same niche and radius as the winning round-3 feature while changing only the cuffing threshold.

variations.name: candidate_variant_a
variations.description: Fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons with at least 2 CA1 reactive astrocytes within 35 µm.

variations.name: candidate_variant_b
variations.description: Fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons with at least 3 CA1 reactive astrocytes within 35 µm.

notes: Use centroid-based neighbor search for efficiency; denominator is all CA1 pyramidal neurons assigned to CA1. Keep the radius fixed at 35 µm to isolate a threshold-change family and avoid repeating the prior any-cuffing feature exactly. Exclude self-matches naturally since source and target cell types differ. Handle donors with very low CA1 pyramidal counts gracefully; if CA1 is missing or denominator is zero, return NaN.
prompt_text:
# Candidate Proposer

You are proposing exactly one candidate biomarker round for an iterative
autoresearch loop.

This system is deliberately simple:

- there is one accepted biomarker panel so far
- each round proposes one new candidate biomarker family
- the worker may test a small local sweep within that candidate family
- the evaluator compares:
  - current accepted panel score
  - panel + candidate score
  - panel with one member replaced by the candidate
- the system then keeps the best reviewed panel only if it improves the train panel score

Your job is only to propose the next candidate.

You will receive a JSON payload containing:

- `program`: the research directive
- `data_summary`: dataset guide
- `accepted_panel`: the current accepted biomarker panel
- `recent_results`: recent keep/discard history from results.tsv
- `round_id`
- `candidate_type`: `seed` if the panel is empty, otherwise `candidate`

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object:

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "short stable slug",
  "scientific_question": "one sentence stating the candidate hypothesis",
  "rationale": "why this candidate is the right next test based on recent results",
  "approach": "how to compute the biomarker from the data",
  "variations": [
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_a",
      "description": "baseline or central parameterization"
    },
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_b",
      "description": "one nearby local change"
    }
  ],
  "baseline_variation": "candidate_variant_a",
  "notes": "data access, coordinate, or implementation notes for the worker"
}
```

## Rules

- Propose exactly one candidate family per round.
- Keep the candidate biologically interpretable.
- If `candidate_type` is `seed`, propose the strongest plausible seed biomarker.
- If `candidate_type` is `candidate`, propose something that could improve the
  accepted panel either by adding new signal or by being a cleaner replacement
  for one weaker existing member.
- Prefer one local family sweep with 2-4 nearby variations, not a grab bag of
  unrelated ideas.
- Use recent results to avoid exact repetition.
- Make the local sweep explicit and small:
  - one radius change
  - one threshold change
  - one local operator change
  - or one biologically coherent gating change
- Do not talk about planners, branches, coordinators, or analyzers.
- Focus on one candidate that is easy to compute and easy to audit.

## Quality bar

A good proposal is:

- specific
- testable in one round
- mechanistically interpretable
- plausibly additive to the accepted panel
- not a vague restatement of the prior winner
